items.title: PgBouncer 1.26.1 released - Fixes three CVEs
items.summary: PgBouncer 1.26.1 has been released. This release fixes three CVEs:CVE-2026-107350: Authentication bypass, allowing a client that knows the password of one SCRAM user to log in as any other SCRAM user, including admins and backend superusers. Caused by a second StartupMessage being processed during SCRAM authentication when connecting to a non-existent database.CVE-2026-107349: DoS due to infinite loop, triggerable by unauthenticated clients. Caused by an empty option name in the startup options parameter, when ignore_startup_parameters is non-empty but does not contain options.CVE-2026-107348: DoS due to infinite loop, triggerable by unauthenticated clients. Caused by an integer overflow in the packet buffer growth logic, only when max_packet_size is set above its default.It also makes ignore_startup_parameters take precedence over tracked parameters, so that ignore_startup_parameters = search_path restores the 1.25 behaviour of ignoring search_path.See https://www.pgbouncer.org/2026/10/pgbouncer-1-26-1 for more information, the detailed changelog, and download links.

items.title: Introducing pglifecycle 2.0 beta
items.summary: I’m pleased to announce the first public release of pglifecycle, an open source schema management tool for PostgreSQL.pglifecycle keeps your database schema in version control as structured YAML, with one file for each table, view, function, role, and other object. This makes the current schema easy to browse, review, and change without reconstructing it from years of migration files.With pglifecycle, you can:Pull an existing database into a schema projectBuild that project into an archive for pg_restoreCompare it with a live database and generate the DDL needed to reconcile themDeployment is plan first. Destructive changes are withheld unless explicitly allowed, making the generated SQL suitable for review in CI.The companion pglifecycle GitHub Action can detect schema drift and post deployment plans directly to pull requests without applying them.Version 2 is a Rust rewrite of the original tool, which has managed AWeber’s production schema for more than seven years. The beta release expands PostgreSQL object coverage and improves deployment convergence and safety.Getting StartedDocumentationGitHub ActionFeedback and real world test cases are welcome as pglifecycle moves toward a stable 2.0 release.
